sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header and date of the maamar for Acharon Shel Pesach 5746.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Acharon Shel Pesach 5746*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse "And My servant Dovid shall be king over them, and they shall all have one shepherd," and raises questions about the future unity under Moshiach from the tribe of Yehudah versus the previous division into two kingdoms.

translations.translation: "And My servant Dovid shall be king over them, and they shall all have one shepherd," etc.1,
And it is known the discourse of the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Nasi of our generation, on the verse2,
which he explains there,
that this verse refers to King Moshiach, who is called by the name Dovid,
Dovid, the King Moshiach.
And the content of the matter is,
that in the future to come, Moshiach will be
(Dovid)
the one shepherd for all of them,
so that they will no longer be divided into two kingdoms3.
For among Israel there were two kingdoms,
the kingdom of the House of Dovid and the kingdom of the House of Yosef
(Ephraim),
for the kings of the House of Dovid were from the tribe of Yehudah and the kings of the House of Yosef were from the tribe of Yosef,
but in the future to come there will no longer be two kingdoms,
rather, one shepherd will be for all of them, and that shepherd will be Dovid,
from the tribe of Yehudah.
And it needs to be understood,
for from the fact that in the future to come there must be a special promise that one shepherd will be for all of them and they will no longer be divided into two kingdoms,
it is understood that even then there is a possibility that there would be two kingdoms,
what is the rationale that in the future to come there would be two kingdoms.
Also, it needs to be understood,
what is the certainty of the superiority in this, that Dovid
(from the tribe of Yehudah)
will be king over them and the one shepherd for all of them,
for ostensibly we find a superiority in Yosef over Yehudah.
For regarding Yosef and Yehudah themselves, behold Yosef was king over all his brothers,
including Yehudah4,
as is explicit in the dreams of Yosef.
And also, there is a superiority in the kingdom of Yosef, which was over ten tribes, unlike the kingdom of Yehudah, which was over only two tribes.
Also, it needs to be understood the content of these matters in the service of man in the present time.
And particularly according to the known principle5
that all the revelations of the future to come depend on our actions and service throughout the time of the exile,
and our Sages, of blessed memory, said6
"Today to do them, and tomorrow to receive their reward."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the difference between Yosef and Yehudah through their names, connecting Yehudah to the power of action and submission, and Yosef to the power of intellect and addition.

translations.translation: And the explanation is7,
for behold, the difference between Yosef and Yehudah will be understood from the names
(Yosef and Yehudah)
themselves,
for Yehudah is from the term "thanksgiving" (hoda'ah) and Yosef is from the term "addition" (hosafah), as is explicit in the verse.
And in the powers of the soul, it is the difference between the power of action in man and the power of intellect within him.
For behold, the power connected with thanksgiving (hoda'ah)
[in people in general
(the speaking species),
and certainly in the children of Israel
(literally a part of G-d above8)]
is the power of action,
for in order for there to be an action in the power of action,
there must be acknowledgment (hoda'ah) and submission.
For the simple meaning of thanksgiving (hoda'ah) is that one acknowledges a certain thing even though it is not understood in his intellect, or moreover, that it is contrary to his intellect9.
For this matter is in the power of action in actuality,
because when a person performs an action, he lowers his will and intellect, etc., until he comes to this action,
and this descent
(in every person,
and particularly in Israel as mentioned above)
is a descent into a deep pit,
therefore there must be within him acknowledgment (hoda'ah) and submission, etc.10
(And this is analogous to the descent of the soul below from a high roof11
to a deep pit,
which descent is in a manner of coercion, as per the statement12
"against your will you live").
However, the matter of addition (hosafah) is the opposite of this.
For addition indicates that the matter is not only received
(settles)
in his intellect,
but furthermore, that through this he adds in wisdom and intellect,
and particularly when there is addition after addition.
For this is the matter of true wisdom and intellect.
And in the powers of man, it is the power of Binah (understanding) within him,
which is called "the expanses of the river"13,
which is in a manner of adding and going and adding,
generating further matters of intellect and reasoning,
for this is the true intent of pilpul (dialectical analysis) and give-and-take, etc.
And it is understood,
that this is the opposite of the matter of coercion and acknowledgment (hoda'ah)
(against your will),
for in the speaking species in general and particularly in Israel,
the intellect is something that is received
(settles),
to the point that one adds in it, etc.
